"Erstelle ein mobiles Fantasy-MMORPG namens AETHERIA mit düsterer Fantasy-Welt, schöner Grafik und Touch-Steuerung.

Klassen @COMMENT_BODY@ Charaktere: Engel oder Dämon als Fraktion, männlich oder weiblich. Klassen: Krieger, Magier und Assassine mit eigenen Waffen, Rüstungen und Fähigkeiten. Charaktername, Frisuren, Haarfarben, Augenfarben und Startoutfits.

Ausrüstung: 9 Ausrüstungsslots, Klassen- und Levelanforderungen. Items haben die Stufen T3, T2 und T1 sowie verschiedene Seltenheiten.

Fusion: 4 identische Items ergeben die nächste Stufe: T3 → T2 → T1 → nächste Seltenheit T3. Kein zufälliges Zerstören. 4 Legendary = Mythic, 4 Mythic = Divine.

Drops: Common 60%, Grey 25%, Green 10%, Blue 5%. Monster droppen immer T3. Purple und höher droppen nicht direkt. Legendary wird gecraftet. Bosssteine haben bis zu 3 Boni. Krit-Chance maximal 50%.

Welt: 8 große Gebiete: Greendale, Ironcrag, Venomwood, Mistgrave, Frostpeak, Sunscorch Desert, Ashen Dominion und Tower of Eternity. Mit Monstern, Elitegegnern, Bossen und Quests. Die ersten 2 Gebiete haben NPCs, spätere nur Rückkehr-Teleporter.

Systeme: Level, XP, Gold, Gems, Quests, Inventar, Lager, Händler, Spielerhandel, Sammeln, Crafting, Schmied und Mounts. Keine Reparaturen.

Flügel: Nur über Quests oder Shop, keine Drops, nicht handelbar oder fusionierbar.

Shop: Kostüme, Frisuren, Mounts, Pets, Waffeneffekte, Flügel und Gems. Free-to-play, Gems auch erspielbar.

Einstellungen: Sprachwahl zwischen Deutsch und Englisch. Das gesamte Spiel muss vollständig übersetzbar sein, einschließlich Menüs, Einstellungen, Quests, Items, NPC-Dialogen, Systemmeldungen und Buttons. Die gewählte Sprache muss gespeichert bleiben und nach einem Neustart erhalten bleiben.

Erstelle ein echtes spielbares Android-Mobilegame mit modularer Struktur, schöner UI, großen Maps und Ladeübergängen. Keine PC-Version. Multiplayer soll später mit echten Servern erweiterbar sein, nicht simuliert werden.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.

- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.

- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.

---
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}"
on:
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Existing issue to run
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);

export function getLang() { return lang; }

export function setLang(next) {
  if (next !== 'de' && next !== 'en') return;
  lang = next;
  document.documentElement.lang = next;
  try { document.documentElement.dataset.lang = next; } catch {}
}

export function t(key, vars) {
  let str = DICT[lang]?.[key] ?? DICT.en?.[key] ?? DICT.de?.[key] ?? key;
  if (vars) {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(vars)) str = str.replaceAll(`{${k}}`, String(v));
  }
  return str;
}

export function tx(value) {
  if (value == null) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  return value[lang] ?? value.en ?? value.de ?? '';
}

export function hasKey(key) {
  return Boolean(DICT[lang]?.[key] || DICT.en?.[key]);
}

export function translationStats() {
  const de = Object.keys(DICT.de).length;
  const en = Object.keys(DICT.en).length;
  const missingEn = Object.keys(DICT.de).filter((k) => !DICT.en[k]);
  const missingDe = Object.keys(DICT.en).filter((k) => !DICT.de[k]);
  return { de, en, missingEn, missingDe };
}

## Objective
- Create a complete, playable, mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG named AETHERIA with touch controls, eight large regions, character progression, inventory/crafting systems, localization, and later multiplayer extensibility.

## Requirements
- Classes: Warrior, Mage, Assassin; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- 9 equipment slots, class/level requirements, T3/T2/T1 tiers, and rarity progression.
- Equipment fusion: 4 identical items advance tier/rarity; 4 Legendary → Mythic and 4 Mythic → Divine; no destruction.
- Monster drops: Common 60%, Grey 25%, Green 10%, Blue 5%; monsters always drop T3; Legendary and higher are crafted; boss stones support up to 3 bonuses; critical chance capped at 50%.
- Eight zones: Greendale, Ironcrag, Venomwood, Mistgrave, Frostpeak, Sunscorch Desert, Ashen Dominion, Tower of Eternity.
- Quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, forge, storage, shops, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable.
- Full German/English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android game, not PC-only; multiplayer must use a real-server-ready seam rather than simulation.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a mobile-first installable web game with an Android/Capacitor wrapper direction.
- Added procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Used browser persistence for settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression.
- Added modular source directories for core systems, data, game engine, UI, and styles.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repository foundation and mobile app shell created.
- Core responsive dark-fantasy UI styling and boot screen added.
- German/English localization core, settings persistence, and save/load system implemented.
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin class data implemented.
- Character appearance data for faction, hairstyles, hair/eye colors, and outfits added.
- Item, rarity, tier, fusion, equipment, crafting, and boss-stone data foundations implemented.
- Eight-zone world data and procedural world generation foundation implemented.
- Quest chain, NPC, shop, mount, pet, wing, and consumable data structures created.
- Procedural hero, monster, terrain, and prop artwork modules created.
- Core player progression, inventory, XP, gold, gems, quests, equipment, and reward logic started.
- Touch/world engine foundation for movement, combat, monsters, gathering, and zone travel created.

### Active
- Completing and validating the playable UI flow and all game screens.
- Verifying world rendering and gameplay loops end-to-end.

### Blocked
- No runtime verification or screenshots are confirmed in the conversation.
- Android signing/build tooling and actual backend multiplayer server implementation are not present yet.

## Next Move
1. Review all created modules for syntax/import issues and finish missing UI screen wiring.
2. Run the app, verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
3. Capture a small JPEG for visual verification and fix rendering/layout issues.
4. Add Android Capacitor packaging and the real multiplayer server/client transport seam.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main application shell and boot screen.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/i18n.js`: Localization dictionary and runtime language switching.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/save.js`: Settings and player save persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/game.js`: Player, progression, inventory, quests, equipment, and economy logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/classes.js`: Factions, classes, appearances, and class abilities.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/items.js`: Items, rarities, tiers, slots, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions and zone properties.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/quests.js`: Quest chains and objectives.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/shop.js`: Shop tabs and purchasable cosmetic/shop content.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/worldgen.js`: Procedural large-zone generation and collisions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/engine.js`: Main gameplay engine for movement, combat, monsters, loot, and travel.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/heroArt.js`: Procedural hero character rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/icons.js`: Shared SVG icon set.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles/base.css`: Global/mobile visual system.

## Important Context
- The implementation is an installable mobile web/PWA foundation with a planned Capacitor Android wrapper, not a completed signed APK.
- Multiplayer is deliberately not implemented as simulated content; it needs a future real-server transport integration.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

- Keep the implementation installable on Android and ready for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server-ready seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Implement as a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the app shell, responsive dark-fantasy styling, localization, persistence, class/character data, items, zones, quests, shops, procedural art, and initial gameplay engine.
- Added `src/core/audio.js` for self-contained procedural audio.
- Added `src/net/tradeClient.js` as a WebSocket transport client seam.
- Added shared UI and screen styles in `src/styles/ui.css` and `src/styles/screens.css`.
- Updated `src/game/engine.js` to localize zone names and equipment names.

### Active
- Review and finish UI screen wiring and verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Check recent audio, multiplayer, styling, and localization changes for integration and syntax issues.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current repository and validate syntax/imports, especially recent additions and the failed final write attempt.
2. Run the app and verify core gameplay flows in a browser; fix visible or functional issues.
3. Capture a small JPEG for visual verification.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main application shell and boot flow.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, and economy logic.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.

- `src/styles/ui.css`: Shared gameplay UI styling.
- `src/styles/screens.css`: Menu and screen styling.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.

- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

export function getLang() { return lang; }

export function setLang(next) {
  if (next !== 'de' && next !== 'en') return;
  lang = next;
  document.documentElement.lang = next;
  try { document.documentElement.dataset.lang = next; } catch {}
}

export function t(key, vars) {
  let str = DICT[lang]?.[key] ?? DICT.en?.[key] ?? DICT.de?.[key] ?? key;
  if (vars) {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(vars)) str = str.replaceAll(`{${k}}`, String(v));
  }
  return str;
}

export function tx(value) {
  if (value == null) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  return value[lang] ?? value.en ?? value.de ?? '';
}

export function hasKey(key) {
  return Boolean(DICT[lang]?.[key] || DICT.en?.[key]);
}

export function translationStats() {
  const de = Object.keys(DICT.de).length;
  const en = Object.keys(DICT.en).length;
  const missingEn = Object.keys(DICT.de).filter((k) => !DICT.en[k]);
  const missingDe = Object.keys(DICT.en).filter((k) => !DICT.de[k]);
  return { de, en, missingEn, missingDe };
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the app shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art, and gameplay engine.
- Added procedural audio in `src/core/audio.js` and a WebSocket client seam in `src/net/tradeClient.js`.
- Updated `src/core/game.js` armor recalculation to include gear `defense` stats.
- Updated `src/game/engine.js` zone loading to capture previous location and restore it only when the destination zone was previously visited.
- Checked existing JavaScript files with `node --check`; no syntax errors were reported before the latest edits.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js` screen/UI wiring and verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Review the recent zone-restore and armor changes for integration correctness.

### Blocked
- A large attempt to create `src/main.js` failed with `tool.input-incomplete` because the write payload exceeded the output token limit; the file’s intended content was not created.
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current repository state and confirm `src/main.js` is absent or incomplete; create it in manageable chunks.
2. Run syntax/import checks after completing UI wiring, then launch and verify core gameplay flows in a browser.
3. Capture and inspect a small screenshot.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell; references `src/main.js`.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, economy, and updated armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and updated zone restoration behavior.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `src/core/save.js`: Settings and player-save persistence.
- `src/data/items.js`: Equipment, rarities, tiers, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions.
- `src/data/quests.js`: Quest chains and objectives.
- `src/game/worldgen.js`: Procedural world generation and collisions.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/styles/ui.css`: Shared gameplay UI styling.
- `src/styles/screens.css`: Menu and screen styling.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; `git status` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, and `src/` as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js`, but the failed write means the application entry point remains unresolved.
- The project is an installable mobile web/PWA foundation, not a completed signed APK; multiplayer still requires a real backend.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built app shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art, gameplay engine, procedural audio, and WebSocket client seam.
- Updated armor recalculation to include gear defense and zone loading to restore position only for previously visited zones.
- Created shared UI helpers in `src/ui/common.js` and screen modules in `src/ui/menu.js`, `src/ui/create.js`, and `src/ui/world.js`.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` controller and integrate the new UI modules.
- Verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Review integration of zone restoration and armor changes.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current repository and new UI modules, then complete `src/main.js` and any missing screens or wiring.
2. Run syntax/import checks and launch the app to verify core gameplay flows.
3. Capture and inspect a small screenshot; address any runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell; references `src/main.js`.
- `src/main.js`: Required entry point; earlier checkpoint says missing, and recent work has not shown it being created.
- `src/ui/common.js`: Shared DOM, toast, modal, formatting, and settings helpers.
- `src/ui/menu.js`: Main menu and settings/credits UI.
- `src/ui/create.js`: Character creation UI.
- `src/ui/world.js`: HUD and world UI integration.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, economy, and armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and zone restoration.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `src/core/save.js`: Settings and player-save persistence.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/data/items.js`: Equipment, rarities, tiers, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions.
- `src/styles/ui.css`: Shared gameplay UI styling.
- `src/styles/screens.css`: Menu and screen styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, and `src/` as untracked.
- The latest UI module writes were reported as completed, but their tool output was truncated; inspect files for completeness and consistency before wiring them.
- The earlier oversized `src/main.js` write failed with `tool.input-incomplete`; no subsequent history confirms successful creation.

export function getLang() { return lang; }

export function setLang(next) {
  if (next !== 'de' && next !== 'en') return;
  lang = next;
  document.documentElement.lang = next;
  try { document.documentElement.dataset.lang = next; } catch {}
}

export function t(key, vars) {
  let str = DICT[lang]?.[key] ?? DICT.en?.[key] ?? DICT.de?.[key] ?? key;
  if (vars) {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(vars)) str = str.replaceAll(`{${k}}`, String(v));
  }
  return str;
}

export function tx(value) {
  if (value == null) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  return value[lang] ?? value.en ?? value.de ?? '';
}

export function hasKey(key) {
  return Boolean(DICT[lang]?.[key] || DICT.en?.[key]);
}

export function translationStats() {
  const de = Object.keys(DICT.de).length;
  const en = Object.keys(DICT.en).length;
  const missingEn = Object.keys(DICT.de).filter((k) => !DICT.en[k]);
  const missingDe = Object.keys(DICT.en).filter((k) => !DICT.de[k]);
  return { de, en, missingEn, missingDe };
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- App shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art/audio, gameplay engine, and WebSocket client seam exist.
- Armor recalculation includes gear defense; zone loading restores position only for previously visited zones.
- Shared UI modules and additional panel modules were written: `src/ui/common.js`, `src/ui/menu.js`, `src/ui/create.js`, `src/ui/world.js`, `src/ui/panelKit.js`, `src/ui/panels.js`, `src/ui/panels/character.js`, `src/ui/panels/quests.js`, and `src/ui/panels/shop.js`.
- Travel confirmation in `src/ui/panels/quests.js` was wired to `confirmDialog` and `panel.screen.travel`.

### Active
- Inspect and integrate new UI modules; complete missing `src/main.js` controller and verify the import graph and UI event wiring.
- Verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Review zone restoration and armor changes in gameplay context.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the panel modules and their exports/imports, then implement or complete `src/main.js` and resolve integration issues.
2. Run syntax/import checks and launch the app to verify core gameplay flows.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot; address runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell; references `src/main.js`.
- `src/main.js`: Required entry point; no successful creation was confirmed.
- `src/ui/panels.js`: Panel orchestration and panel actions.
- `src/ui/panelKit.js`: Shared panel rendering helpers.
- `src/ui/panels/character.js`: Character, inventory, mounts, wardrobe, and storage views.
- `src/ui/panels/quests.js`: Quest journal and world map.
- `src/ui/panels/shop.js`: Cosmetic shop, daily gift, and merchant.
- `src/ui/common.js`: Shared DOM, toast, modal, formatting, and settings helpers.
- `src/ui/menu.js`: Main menu and settings/credits UI.
- `src/ui/create.js`: Character creation UI.
- `src/ui/world.js`: HUD and world integration.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, economy, and armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and zone restoration.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier status showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, and `src/` as untracked.
- The latest module writes were reported as completed, but tool output was truncated; inspect files for completeness and consistency before wiring.
- Runtime verification and screenshots remain unconfirmed.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

We'll call recalc(player) then game = createGame? createGame uses player.createdAt which is Date.now number. saved.createdAt. `createGame` sets createdAt = player.createdAt (timestamp of player creation) not save.createdAt; acceptable. But loses savedAt. Better construct game manually or `createGame` then set createdAt=saved.createdAt. Need stable.

## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Equipment progression, crafting, quests, eight regions, mounts, gathering, shops, storage, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- App shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art/audio, gameplay engine, and WebSocket client seam exist.
- UI modules for shared components, menu, character creation, world HUD, and panels exist.
- Added `src/ui/panels/forge.js` and `src/ui/panels/trade.js`; connected trade cleanup through `src/ui/panels.js`.
- Added `src/main.js` as the application controller for boot, menus, character creation, world HUD, panels, and persistence.
- Adjusted modal close handling and persistent language selection.

### Active
- Validate new controller and panel integration, including trade behavior and boot-to-game flow.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `src/main.js`, `src/ui/panels/forge.js`, and `src/ui/panels/trade.js` for integration issues and verify syntax/import checks.
2. Launch the app and test boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop/forge/trade flows.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot; address runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: New app controller and entry point.
- `src/ui/panels.js`: Panel orchestration, actions, and trade cleanup.
- `src/ui/panels/forge.js`: Fusion, crafting, and blacksmith UI.
- `src/ui/panels/trade.js`: WebSocket-backed player trade UI.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, economy, equipment, and armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and zone restoration.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `index.html`: App shell and entry-point reference.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Static syntax and import checks were invoked, but their results are not confirmed in the available history.
- Runtime verification and screenshots remain unconfirmed.
